tagline: From Hangtown up the South Fork to Echo Summit.
intro: Out of Placerville, called Hangtown in 1849, US 50 runs east past Pollock Pines and reaches the canyon of the South Fork American River at Riverton. From there it is mostly two lanes, rising steadily beside the river past Kyburz and Strawberry, then up a grade of hairpin turns to Echo Summit, 7,382 feet, where US 50 tops out in California. Over the top it eases down a steep hillside into the Lake Tahoe Basin.

Forty-niners came this way, and so did the Pony Express. In 1895 part of the road became California's first state highway, and in 1910 the state started sprinkling it with water in summer to keep down the dust.

moments.title: Kyburz
moments.text: Slippery Ford until 1896 and Slipperyford until 1911, when the postmaster renamed it for his father, an early pioneer who had been with John Sutter.

moments.title: Strawberry
moments.text: A resort in the 1850s and a Pony Express station, now a highway sign reading population 50 and the Lovers Leap climbing area.

moments.title: Echo Summit
moments.text: In 1968 the men's Olympic track trials were run up here, on a track laid in a ski-area parking lot with Ponderosa pines left standing in the infield.

sources.label: Wikipedia, Strawberry, El Dorado County, California
